chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Mashriqi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Qays, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: 'Nay, both His Hands are spread out.' So I asked him, 'Does He have hands like this?' and I pointed with my hand to his hand. He replied, 'No, for if that were the case, He would have been created.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Allah's Hands in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) uses the gesture of pointing to his own physical hand to illustrate that if Allah’s 'Hands' were identical in form to created limbs, they would be contingent beings rather than eternal attributes. This hadith serves as a foundational argument in Shia theology for *tanzih* (divine transcendence), distinguishing between literal bodily parts (*ajza'*) and eternal divine attributes (*sifat*) to avoid anthropomorphism (*tashbih*).
